item.title: What Is Next After the Suicide Attack in Pakistan?
item.description: This morning, a suicide bomber attacked a Shia mosque in Islamabad, Pakistan. The most likely perpetrator is the Islamic State–Khorasan Province, which operates both in Afghanistan and Pakistan but has a significant interest in mass-casualty international attacks.

item.title: CSIS Global Health Policy Center Names Ambassador Lisa Carty Non-Resident Senior Adviser
item.description: The Center for Strategic and International Studies (CSIS) today announced that Ambassador (retired) Lisa Carty has been appointed as a non-resident senior adviser with the CSIS Global Health Policy Center (GHPC).

item.title: Tracking China’s Increased Military Activities in the Indo-Pacific in 2025
item.description: Analysis of open-source data shows that China’s military activities in the Indo-Pacific region increased in both operational tempo and geographical reach.

item.title: States Weekly: February 4, 2026
item.description: This edition of States Weekly covers February 4, 2026.

item.title: Where Sovereignty Meets Statecraft: South Korea’s Fairness Act and the U.S. Alliance
item.description: The Fairness Act will test whether the United States and South Korea can manage regulatory differences without sacrificing strategic cooperation. How Washington responds will signal to allies worldwide whether legitimate domestic governance invites trade retaliation.

item.title: Nearshoring Without Growth: Why Investment Uncertainty Is Holding Mexico Back
item.description: CSIS Americas Fellow Diego Marroquin Bitar and Director Ryan C. Berg analyze how investment uncertainty is keeping Mexico from realizing its economic potential amid global trade tensions.
